items.stem: What is meant by "Entrepreneurial opportunity"?
items.answer: A favourable set of circumstances that creates a need for a new product, service or business.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A favourable set of circumstances that creates a need for a new product, service or business.

items.stem: Explain "Natural resources" with reference to the idea fields for spotting business ideas.
items.answer: Natural resources: Ideas based on local raw materials, such as fruit processing, bamboo crafts or herbal products.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Ideas based on local raw materials, such as fruit processing, bamboo crafts or herbal products.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about sensing entrepreneurial opportunities is NOT correct?
items.answer: Every idea is automatically a business opportunity.
items.markingKey: (d) Incorrect statement: Every idea is automatically a business opportunity.
options: Natural resources, knowledge and trends are idea fields.
Unmet customer needs are a source of opportunities.
An opportunity window does not remain open for ever.
Every idea is automatically a business opportunity.

items.stem: Aditi added a built-in water filter to an ordinary steel bottle and sold it as a new product. Which idea field has the entrepreneur used?
items.answer: Existing products and services
items.markingKey: (d) Existing products and services. It improves an existing product.

items.stem: Vihaan, a software engineer, started a firm that builds billing apps for small shops. Which idea field has the entrepreneur used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Knowledge. The idea is based on technical expertise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Knowledge; 2 marks for the justification: The idea is based on technical expertise.

items.stem:
Arjun noticed that many working parents in Jaipur had no time to cook healthy meals. Being a trained nutritionist, he started a subscription service delivering balanced lunch boxes, using vegetables from nearby farms.
(i) Identify the idea fields Arjun used. (ii) State three factors that helped him sense the opportunity.
items.answer: (i) Trends (busy lifestyles); knowledge (nutrition); natural resources (local vegetables). (ii) Market and customer needs; knowledge and experience; availability of resources; creativity (any three).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Trends (busy lifestyles); knowledge (nutrition); natural resources (local vegetables). (ii) Market and customer needs; knowledge and experience; availability of resources; creativity (any three).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about sensing entrepreneurial opportunities is correct?
items.answer: An opportunity window does not remain open for ever.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: An opportunity window does not remain open for ever.
options: Every idea is automatically a business opportunity.
Knowledge cannot be the basis of a business.
Opportunities exist only in large cities.
An opportunity window does not remain open for ever.

items.stem: Sneha uses bamboo from the forests of the North-East to make furniture. Which idea field has the entrepreneur used?
items.answer: Natural resources
items.markingKey: (a) Natural resources. Local raw material is used.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Dev, a software engineer, started a firm that builds billing apps for small shops. (a) Which idea field has the entrepreneur used? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Knowledge (b) The idea is based on technical expertise.
items.markingKey: (a) Knowledge, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: The idea is based on technical expertise.

items.stem: State any three benefits of environment scanning for an entrepreneur.
items.answer: Identifies opportunities; Gives early warning of threats; Helps in planning; Improves decision-making; Helps the enterprise adapt
items.markingKey: Any three of: Identifies opportunities; Gives early warning of threats; Helps in planning; Improves decision-making; Helps the enterprise adapt (1 mark each).

items.stem: State one difference between strengths and weaknesses and opportunities and threats on the basis of example.
items.answer: strengths and weaknesses: skilled staff; poor location; opportunities and threats: rising demand; new competitor
items.markingKey: 1 mark: strengths and weaknesses: skilled staff; poor location; opportunities and threats: rising demand; new competitor

items.stem: Distinguish between strengths and weaknesses and opportunities and threats on the basis of control, example and source.
items.answer: (i) Control: strengths and weaknesses: largely within the control of the entrepreneur; opportunities and threats: outside the control of the entrepreneur. (ii) Example: strengths and weaknesses: skilled staff; poor location; opportunities and threats: rising demand; new competitor. (iii) Source: strengths and weaknesses: internal to the business; opportunities and threats: external to the business.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Control: strengths and weaknesses: largely within the control of the entrepreneur; opportunities and threats: outside the control of the entrepreneur. (ii) Example: strengths and weaknesses: skilled staff; poor location; opportunities and threats: rising demand; new competitor. (iii) Source: strengths and weaknesses: internal to the business; opportunities and threats: external to the business.

items.stem: A ban on single-use plastic has increased the demand for cloth and paper bags. Which PESTLE factor is involved?
items.answer: Environmental
items.markingKey: (d) Environmental. It relates to pollution norms.

items.stem: More young people in Indore prefer to eat out on weekends. Which PESTLE factor is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Social. It is a change in lifestyle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Social; 2 marks for the justification: It is a change in lifestyle.

items.stem: Bose Agencies has an old machine that often breaks down. In a SWOT analysis, what type of factor is this? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Weakness. It is an internal disadvantage.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Weakness; 2 marks for the justification: It is an internal disadvantage.

items.stem:
Ananya plans a cloud kitchen in Mysuru. She has cooking skills but limited funds. Food delivery apps are growing fast, but two big chains have just opened outlets nearby, and new hygiene rules are coming.
(i) Prepare a SWOT analysis for Ananya's idea. (ii) Which PESTLE factor do the new hygiene rules represent?
items.answer: (i) Strength: cooking skills; weakness: limited funds; opportunity: growth of food delivery apps; threat: big chains nearby. (ii) Legal.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Strength: cooking skills; weakness: limited funds; opportunity: growth of food delivery apps; threat: big chains nearby. (ii) Legal.

items.stem:
Om plans a cloud kitchen in Bhopal. He has cooking skills but limited funds. Food delivery apps are growing fast, but two big chains have just opened outlets nearby, and new hygiene rules are coming.
(i) Prepare a SWOT analysis for Om's idea. (ii) Which PESTLE factor do the new hygiene rules represent?
items.answer: (i) Strength: cooking skills; weakness: limited funds; opportunity: growth of food delivery apps; threat: big chains nearby. (ii) Legal.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Strength: cooking skills; weakness: limited funds; opportunity: growth of food delivery apps; threat: big chains nearby. (ii) Legal.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The process of collecting and analysing information about the external environment to spot opportunities and threats."
items.answer: Environment scanning
items.markingKey: (c) Environment scanning: The process of collecting and analysing information about the external environment to spot opportunities and threats.

items.stem: Rao Traders has a team of highly skilled designers. In a SWOT analysis, what type of factor is this?
items.answer: Strength
items.markingKey: (a) Strength. It is an internal advantage.

items.stem:
Varun wants to start an electric-scooter rental business in Guwahati. The government gives subsidies on electric vehicles, fuel prices are rising, young people prefer shared transport, battery technology is improving, and pollution norms are getting stricter.
(i) Classify each fact under a PESTLE factor and say whether the environment favours the idea.
items.answer: (i) Political: subsidies; economic: rising fuel prices; social: preference for shared transport; technological: better batteries; environmental: stricter pollution norms. Yes, the environment is favourable.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Political: subsidies; economic: rising fuel prices; social: preference for shared transport; technological: better batteries; environmental: stricter pollution norms. Yes, the environment is favourable.

items.stem: State any three sources of ideas for a new venture.
items.answer: Customers' complaints and feedback; Existing products and services; Trade fairs and exhibitions; Media and the internet; Research and development; Personal experience and hobbies
items.markingKey: Any three of: Customers' complaints and feedback; Existing products and services; Trade fairs and exhibitions; Media and the internet; Research and development; Personal experience and hobbies (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Personal experience and hobbies" with reference to the sources of ideas for a new venture.
items.answer: Personal experience and hobbies: Problems faced by the entrepreneur suggest solutions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Problems faced by the entrepreneur suggest solutions.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about idea generation is NOT correct?
items.answer: Demand is not considered while selecting an idea.
items.markingKey: (d) Incorrect statement: Demand is not considered while selecting an idea.
options: A mind map has a central idea with branches.
Demand is not considered while selecting an idea.

items.stem: Farhan drew a diagram with 'eco-friendly travel' in the middle and linked it to cycles, electric scooters and car-pooling. Which technique of idea generation is being used?
items.answer: Mind-mapping
items.markingKey: (b) Mind-mapping. Related ideas branch from the central idea.

items.stem:
Fatima kept getting complaints from customers that her paper bags tear when wet. She began developing a bag with a thin waterproof coating.
(i) What source of idea did Fatima use? (ii) Which step of the process does this show?
items.answer: (i) Customers' complaints and feedback. (ii) Problem identification leading to idea generation.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Customers' complaints and feedback. (ii) Problem identification leading to idea generation.

items.stem:
Students of a school in Jaipur wanted to start a small business. They first listed every idea anyone could think of without judging, then drew a chart around 'school needs', and finally compared the ideas on demand, resources and profit.
(i) Identify the three steps or techniques used. (ii) State two rules of the first technique. (iii) State one more criterion they could use.
items.answer: (i) Brainstorming; mind-mapping; screening and selection of ideas. (ii) No criticism; quantity is welcome; wild ideas encouraged; build on others' ideas (any two). (iii) Competition / risk involved / personal interest and skills.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Brainstorming; mind-mapping; screening and selection of ideas. (ii) No criticism; quantity is welcome; wild ideas encouraged; build on others' ideas (any two). (iii) Competition / risk involved / personal interest and skills.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Varun and his friends sat together and called out as many ideas as possible for a college start-up, writing all of them on a board without judging any. (a) Which technique of idea generation is being used? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Brainstorming (b) Free group suggestion without criticism.
items.markingKey: (a) Brainstorming, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Free group suggestion without criticism.

items.stem: State any three rules of brainstorming.
items.answer: No criticism of ideas; Quantity is welcome; Wild ideas are encouraged; Build on the ideas of others
items.markingKey: Any three of: No criticism of ideas; Quantity is welcome; Wild ideas are encouraged; Build on the ideas of others (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Creativity"?
items.answer: The ability to produce new and useful ideas.
items.markingKey: (d) Creativity: The ability to produce new and useful ideas.
options: A group technique in which members freely suggest as many ideas as possible without criticism.
A diagram that places a central idea in the middle with related ideas branching out from it.
Comparing ideas against criteria to drop the weak ones and keep the promising ones.
The ability to produce new and useful ideas.

items.stem: State any three points examined in financial feasibility.
items.answer: Total cost of the project; Sources of funds; Expected sales and profit; Break-even point; Return on investment
items.markingKey: Any three of: Total cost of the project; Sources of funds; Expected sales and profit; Break-even point; Return on investment (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Sources of funds" with reference to the points examined in financial feasibility.
items.answer: Sources of funds: Owner's capital, loans and investors.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Owner's capital, loans and investors.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): An idea becomes an opportunity once it is shown to be feasible.
Reason (R): Every feasible idea is guaranteed to succeed.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true; R is false: feasibility lowers risk but does not guarantee success.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Diya surveys colleges in Dehradun to estimate how many students would use a laundry app. Which type of feasibility is being studied?
items.answer: Market feasibility
items.markingKey: (a) Market feasibility. Size of the market is examined.

items.stem:
Ishaan found that customers want low-cost solar lamps, but the solar cells he needs are not available locally and must be imported at a high cost.
(i) Which type of feasibility is weak? (ii) Suggest one way to deal with it.
items.answer: (i) Technical feasibility (also financial, due to high cost). (ii) Find another supplier or technology, import in bulk, or tie up with a manufacturer.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Technical feasibility (also financial, due to high cost). (ii) Find another supplier or technology, import in bulk, or tie up with a manufacturer.

items.stem: Lakshmi checks whether skilled weavers and good-quality yarn are available near her proposed unit. Which type of feasibility is being studied? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Technical feasibility. Raw material and manpower are examined.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Technical feasibility; 2 marks for the justification: Raw material and manpower are examined.

items.stem:
Pooja wants to start a unit making millet-based snacks in Patna. She has found suppliers of millets and a suitable machine, estimates a project cost of ₹12 lakh, and believes health-conscious young people will buy the snacks.
(i) Identify the three types of feasibility in the case. (ii) What else should she check under market feasibility?
items.answer: (i) Technical (suppliers, machine); financial (project cost); market (health-conscious buyers). (ii) Size of the market, competition, price customers will pay, distribution.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Technical (suppliers, machine); financial (project cost); market (health-conscious buyers). (ii) Size of the market, competition, price customers will pay, distribution.

items.stem:
Sahil wants to start a unit making millet-based snacks in Lucknow. He has found suppliers of millets and a suitable machine, estimates a project cost of ₹12 lakh, and believes health-conscious young people will buy the snacks.

items.answer: (i) Technical (suppliers, machine); financial (project cost); market (health-conscious buyers). (ii) Size of the market, competition, price customers will pay, distribution.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Technical (suppliers, machine); financial (project cost); market (health-conscious buyers). (ii) Size of the market, competition, price customers will pay, distribution.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about feasibility of a business idea is correct?
items.answer: Technical feasibility examines technology and raw material.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: Technical feasibility examines technology and raw material.
options: Technical feasibility examines technology and raw material.
A feasibility study is done after the business starts.
Financial feasibility examines only the colour of the product.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about feasibility of a business idea is NOT correct?
items.answer: Financial feasibility examines only the colour of the product.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: Financial feasibility examines only the colour of the product.
options: A feasibility study reduces the risk of failure.
Market feasibility examines demand and competition.
Financial feasibility examines only the colour of the product.
Technical feasibility examines technology and raw material.

items.stem: Distinguish between an idea and an opportunity on the basis of meaning, value and test.
items.answer: (i) Meaning: an idea: a thought about a possible product or service; an opportunity: an idea with real demand that can be met profitably. (ii) Value: an idea: may or may not be workable; an opportunity: commercially workable. (iii) Test: an idea: not yet tested; an opportunity: tested for feasibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Meaning: an idea: a thought about a possible product or service; an opportunity: an idea with real demand that can be met profitably. (ii) Value: an idea: may or may not be workable; an opportunity: commercially workable. (iii) Test: an idea: not yet tested; an opportunity: tested for feasibility.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Rising interest rates increased the cost of loans for small firms in Nagpur. (a) Which PESTLE factor is involved? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Economic (b) Interest rates are an economic factor.
items.markingKey: (a) Economic, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Interest rates are an economic factor.

items.stem: Explain "Availability of resources" with reference to the factors involved in sensing entrepreneurial opportunities.
items.answer: Availability of resources: Access to raw material, skills and funds makes an idea workable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Access to raw material, skills and funds makes an idea workable.

items.answer: Whether the project can raise the funds needed and earn an adequate return.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Whether the project can raise the funds needed and earn an adequate return.

items.answer: An external factor that the business can use to its advantage.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: An external factor that the business can use to its advantage.

items.stem:
Aisha found that tourists visiting her hill town could not find locally made souvenirs. She started a shop selling wooden crafts made by local artisans.
(i) Which idea field is shown? (ii) What made it an opportunity and not just an idea?
items.answer: (i) Demand and market gaps (also natural resources: local wood). (ii) There was real unmet demand from tourists, and resources (artisans, wood) were available.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Demand and market gaps (also natural resources: local wood). (ii) There was real unmet demand from tourists, and resources (artisans, wood) were available.

items.answer: Raw material: Its availability, quality and cost.

items.stem:
Aditya noticed that many working parents in Lucknow had no time to cook healthy meals. Being a trained nutritionist, he started a subscription service delivering balanced lunch boxes, using vegetables from nearby farms.
(i) Identify the idea fields Aditya used. (ii) State three factors that helped him sense the opportunity.
items.answer: (i) Trends (busy lifestyles); knowledge (nutrition); natural resources (local vegetables). (ii) Market and customer needs; knowledge and experience; availability of resources; creativity (any three).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Trends (busy lifestyles); knowledge (nutrition); natural resources (local vegetables). (ii) Market and customer needs; knowledge and experience; availability of resources; creativity (any three).

items.stem: Explain "Distribution" with reference to the points examined in market feasibility.
items.answer: Distribution: How the product will reach customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: How the product will reach customers.

items.stem:
Varun kept getting complaints from customers that his paper bags tear when wet. He began developing a bag with a thin waterproof coating.
(i) What source of idea did Varun use? (ii) Which step of the process does this show?
items.answer: (i) Customers' complaints and feedback. (ii) Problem identification leading to idea generation.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Customers' complaints and feedback. (ii) Problem identification leading to idea generation.

items.stem: Explain "Improves decision-making" with reference to the benefits of environment scanning for an entrepreneur.
items.answer: Improves decision-making: Choices are based on information, not guesswork.
